prompt.context: Your client is a large pharmaceutical company that will be launching a new drug for the well-known illness, MBAitis. Their drug, Blue Devil Serum (BDS) is a high efficacy alternative to current therapies, and will launch in the next 18-24 months.
prompt.question: What should they consider in planning the launch to maximize revenue over the first 3 years?

clarifying_info.a: Yes, it is a multinational company with many different drugs across diseases.

clarifying_info.q: Which geographic markets should we consider?
clarifying_info.a: Your team is hired to consider the US context only.

clarifying_info.q: Does the company have manufacturing and supply chain capabilities?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the company already has a well-established manufacturing and supply chain.

clarifying_info.q: Does the company sell any other MBAitis drugs?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, they sell other MBAitis drugs, including one that is potentially a direct competitor to BDS.

exhibits.title: Market size and revenue estimates for BDS 2017-2024
exhibits.shows: Two triangles showing the percent of total drug prescriptions going to each MBAitis patient segment for MBI (client's existing drug) and BDS (new drug), plus a line chart of projected revenue for MBI and BDS from 2017 to 2024 in $M.

data.note: MBI (Myrtle Beach Injection) is a lower efficacy and lower risk therapy compared to BDS. Revenue chart shows MBI declining steadily and BDS growing from 2017 to 2024.

exhibits.title: Profits associated with salesforce options
exhibits.shows: A table comparing three salesforce options (A: Single salesforce MBI/BDS, B: Two separate salesforces, C: Two separate salesforces + CSO) across number of FTE increases, cost per FTE, and FTE-driven increase in revenue as a percent of FTE cost for Years 1, 2, and 3.

data.note: CSO = Contract Sales Organization (external vendor to help with sales)

framework: Market and patient landscape: Understand MBAitis patient segments (first diagnosis, early, mid, advanced, relapse, terminal), total addressable market, and competitive dynamics
Product differentiation: Assess BDS efficacy vs. existing therapies (including client's own MBI drug); identify target patient segments for BDS vs. MBI
Cannibalization risk: Quantify overlap between BDS and MBI target segments; determine revenue at risk from internal cannibalization
Go-to-market strategy: Pricing, salesforce structure, marketing channels, messaging to doctors and patients
Revenue maximization levers: Salesforce optimization, ad campaigns, new patient channels, brand positioning

questions.prompt: Examine Exhibit 1. What does it tell you about the relationship between BDS and MBI, and what is the implication for the client?
questions.guidance: A good candidate recognizes: (1) MBI accounts for the bulk of company revenue but is declining steadily through 2024. (2) BDS and MBI have ~30% overlap in target patient segments (both drugs are prescribed to first diagnosis, early, and relapse patients). (3) Introducing BDS will cannibalize MBI revenue. A great candidate further quantifies: BDS will cannibalize 30% of MBI revenue; MBI revenue is declining ~5% per year; BDS must generate enough incremental revenue to offset that loss. Candidate should use language of 'patients' not 'customers.'

math.setup: MBI revenue is declining 5% per year. BDS will cannibalize 30% of MBI revenue on top of this organic decline. The candidate should estimate how much BDS needs to generate annually to offset MBI revenue loss.
steps: Identify that MBI and BDS overlap in ~30% of patient segments (first diagnosis, early, relapse)
Recognize MBI revenue declining ~5%/year (visible from the revenue chart trend)
Conclude BDS revenue must exceed cannibalization loss plus organic MBI decline to net positive for the company
math.answer: BDS must generate revenue greater than the 30% cannibalized from MBI plus the ongoing ~5%/year MBI decline to be net revenue positive for the company.

questions.prompt: Having recognized that BDS will be a direct competitor for a certain segment of patients already covered by MBI, what are some ways to mitigate this cannibalization?
questions.guidance: Candidate should produce a structured brainstorm. Key areas: salesforce strategy (separate salesforces to market drugs to distinct segments), advertising and messaging (differentiate BDS vs. MBI to patients and doctors, use new media), new patient channels (apps, personalized medicine, field nurses, educational programming), brand repositioning of MBI to non-overlapping segments. Guide toward salesforce structure as a key lever.

questions.prompt: The client is evaluating 3 salesforce options (Exhibit 2). Which option should they choose, and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate total 3-year revenue, total 3-year cost, and total 3-year profit for each option. A good candidate calculates correctly. A great candidate remembers the goal is maximizing revenue (not profit) and recommends Option B despite comparable profit to Option A, because it yields the highest total revenue over 3 years.

math.setup: For each option: Annual FTE cost = Increase in FTEs x Cost/FTE. Annual FTE-driven revenue = Annual FTE cost x FTE-driven revenue pct. Compute for each year, then sum over 3 years.
math.answer: Option B yields the highest total 3-year revenue ($9,585,000) and the highest total 3-year profit ($1,485,000). Since the client's goal is to maximize revenue, Option B (two separate salesforces) is recommended.

brainstorming.prompt: What are some ways to mitigate cannibalization of MBI by BDS?

categories.name: Salesforce structure
ideas: Use separate salesforces for MBI and BDS to target distinct patient segments
Develop differentiated messaging and training for each salesforce
Minimize cross-promotion between the two drugs

categories.name: Advertising and brand messaging
ideas: Adjust ad campaigns to differentiate BDS from MBI for both patients and doctors
Reposition MBI brand to emphasize non-overlapping patient segments (e.g., advanced, terminal)
Explore new media outlets to reach distinct audiences

categories.name: New patient channels
ideas: Reach new patients through digital channels and apps
Introduce personalized medicine approaches such as field nurses or patient liaisons
Develop educational programming to expand overall market rather than just shifting existing patients

recommendation: The client should pursue Option B — two separate salesforces — for the launch of BDS, which yields projected incremental revenue of approximately $9.6M over 3 years, the highest of all options evaluated.
Separate salesforces allow differentiated messaging to minimize cannibalization of MBI, while maximizing BDS patient reach.
risks: Cannibalization rate could far exceed projections even with separate salesforces if messaging overlap persists
MBI revenue may decline faster than the 5%/year projected, reducing the net benefit of the BDS launch
Ramp-up time for two separate salesforces may delay revenue realization in Year 1
next_steps: Develop distinct brand positioning and training for each salesforce to minimize overlap
Monitor MBI revenue trajectory and adjust salesforce allocation if cannibalization exceeds 30%
Explore new patient acquisition channels (apps, field nurses) to grow overall MBAitis market
